core.title: Normalize operator replies to keep/pivot/kill and confirm unclear intent
core.given: During decomposition the operator replies to a keep/pivot/kill decision, in prose or in decision words, and the reply needs interpretation.
core.when: The planner records the operator's decision and proceeds.
core.then: Normalize the reply to exactly one of keep, pivot or kill, and for pivot name the modification the operator asked for.
prefer: Accept free-text replies; map them onto keep/pivot/kill instead of demanding the operator retype a keyword.

Whenever the interpretation is ambiguous, whatever the reply format, restate your interpretation (the normalized decision, plus the named modification for pivot) and get the operator's confirmation before acting on it.
avoid: Proceeding on an ambiguous interpretation of the operator's reply without restating it and confirming first.
Recording a pivot without naming the modification it implies.
core.why: The operator may answer in prose, so the reply must be normalized to keep/pivot/kill to be recorded as a decision; restating and confirming unclear intent avoids acting on a misread interpretation.
evidence: Each operator reply interpreted as a decision is followed by a recorded normalized decision of keep, pivot or kill.
Every recorded pivot carries a named modification.
Where the interpretation was ambiguous (regardless of prose or literal format), the transcript shows the planner restating its interpretation and the operator confirming before the planner proceeded.
verification: The check verifies normalization: every operator reply interpreted as a keep/pivot/kill decision is recorded as exactly one of keep, pivot (with a named modification) or kill; the normalized output vocabulary is closed.
The check verifies ambiguity confirmation: on any unclear intent, whatever the reply format (not only prose), the interpretation was restated and the operator confirmed before the planner acted.

Activation is not deterministic today: the decision phase needs a new observer (the planner being in decomposition and interpreting an operator reply as a keep/pivot/kill decision), and whether a reply needs normalization or is ambiguous is LLM-judged; reply format alone does not decide ambiguity.

values: operator reply to be interpreted as keep/pivot/kill (prose or decision word)

fires: The operator answers in prose and the planner must map the reply onto keep, pivot or kill.
The operator's reply implies changing the item, so it must be recorded as pivot with a named modification.
The operator's reply could plausibly mean more than one of keep/pivot/kill.
The operator replies with a literal decision word but the intended modification is unclear.
doesNotFire: The operator's reply is a genuinely unambiguous keep, kill, or pivot with an explicit modification that needs no interpretation or normalization.
Operator messages that are not a reply to be interpreted as a keep/pivot/kill decision (e.g. general questions or new requirements).

classification.note: Fully stack-neutral: names only the decomposition phase, the operator and the keep/pivot/kill decision vocabulary, which are the subject of the obligation itself.

The single obligation (normalize + named modification for pivot); the second obligation (confirm on ambiguity) is deliberately kept out of then and carried by prefer[1]/avoid[0]/evidence[2], mirroring bun.json.
Role-level preference: accept free-text and map it; no stack or file specifics.
Second obligation expressed as a preference; applies to any ambiguous reply regardless of format.
Negative restatement of the confirm-before-acting obligation.
Negative restatement of the named-modification-for-pivot obligation.
Transcript-observable check; 'transcript' is a neutral dialogue artifact, not a stack path.
Neutral; the 'regardless of prose or literal format' scope is preserved.

The definition of normalization maps to the core's first verification entry; the quoted term id 'normalization' is a source/realization label and stays with the Bun sidecar, but its meaning is stack-neutral, so nothing is bunOnly.
The definition of ambiguity confirmation maps to the core's second verification entry; the term id 'ambiguity_confirm' remains a realization label.
Closed output vocabulary, ambiguity scope beyond prose, and non-deterministic activation (needs_new_observer + llm_judged) all map verbatim in meaning to the core's verification entries.
Phase fact; the observer requirement is carried by observability needs_new_observer and restated in core verification.
Task-term fact; LLM-judged observability preserved; the note that reply format alone does not decide ambiguity is preserved in verification and prefer[1].

neutralityNotes: The whole convention is a planner-operator dialogue behavior with no structural dependency on any stack: it names no runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path, so the core is a faithful neutral restatement of bun.json and no profileRequirements or bunOnly items exist. 'Planner', 'operator' and the closed keep/pivot/kill decision vocabulary are process roles and terms intrinsic to the obligation, not stack constructs, so they stay in the core text itself (task terms belong to core activation or the realization per the vocabulary's notProfileKeys). Two sidecar-level details stay with the Bun realization and were not classified as items: the term ids 'normalization'/'ambiguity_confirm' (labels whose meanings are folded into core verification) and the splitSuggestion for planner.decomposition.ambiguity-confirm (bookkeeping for the second obligation, which the core keeps as prefer[1]/avoid[0]/evidence[2] exactly as bun.json does, so the obligation set is unchanged).
